refutations.evidence: A is the unused upper part of the VDP1 command-list buffer, which can grow. Its lower edge is the highest point seen so far, not a fixed structural limit. Base pointer: *0x06047D1C = 0x060E1000. Current pointer: 0x060CE668. The per-frame flush is at 0x0600FF7C-0x0600FF8E. It sets size = *0x060CE668 - 0x060E1000, SCU-DMAs that many bytes to VRAM 0x25C00000 through 0x0603D22C, and keeps the largest size seen at 0x06047D30. The appenders write a 32-byte command at the current pointer and then do `add #32,r3; mov.l r3,@r14` with no bound check: 0x06011684-0x06011688, 0x06011324-0x06011328, 0x0601F030 onward, 0x0601F788 onward, 0x0602ABA8 onward. The overlays OPDEMO, STG0AS, END, VICTORY and M2CB0E/M3CB0E (A and B) also use 0x060CE668. No literal compares the current pointer against any 0x060E3xxx-0x060E8000 limit. Evidence in local/opt001/wramh_27173.bin (Options screen): *0x06047D30 = 0x2300, and the end command 0x80000000 sits at 0x060E32E0. 0x060E1000 + 0x2300 = 0x060E3300, and A starts at 0x060E32E4, 4 bytes after the end command's first long. So the start of A is exactly the observed peak. In every fight and ending dump (end001, end002, end010, loc001, loc002) the peak is only 0x0A20-0x13E0. The next region up is the pattern-staging base *0x06047D20 = 0x060E8000, and patterns go to VRAM 0x25C08000, so the design leaves room for commands up to 0x060E8000. Any frame with more than about 279 commands would write into A, and the flush DMA would also read A. A likely trigger is a translated Options screen or text screen that draws more glyph sprites.

B's limits come from leftovers, not from a layout. The lower edge 0x060DF8A8 is the linker _end. Startup at 0x0600D3B0-0x0600D408 clears 0x060DF784-0x060DF8A8 and 0x060CC000-0x060DF784, and copies zero bytes to 0x060DF8A8, using the tables at 0x06045208 and 0x06047008. No other code references these tables, so there is no heap above _end. The upper edge 0x060E0EA4 is the lowest point reached by 0.BIN's stack. 0.BIN loads at 0x060A0000-0x060E2608 and its entry sets r15 = 0x060E1144 (literal at file offset 0xC). The stale frames at 0x060E0EA7-0x060E1144 hold return addresses 0x060AADF2, 0x060B066C and 0x060AA8BC, and they are identical in all 18 WRAM-H dumps, including the boot ones. CYBER.BIN never names 0.BIN, so this stack is not reused, but B's size is that boot program's low-water mark. Loader caps (maximums, not real file sizes): table loads to 0x06060000 with r6 = 0x80000 (0x060388FA, 0x06038B9C, 0x06038BCA) could reach 0x060E0000, which covers 0x060DF8A8-0x060DFFFF. CB loads to 0x06070800 and 0x0608B000 with an 0x80000 cap (0x06038830, 0x0603886C) could cover all of B and A. Actual sizes are small: STG0AS 0x4E4D4, END 0x4DBE8, M2CB/M3CB at most 0x19B3C. So B is at risk only if a patched overlay grows a lot, and such an overlay would hit BSS at 0x060CC000 first. The literals 0x060E0000 and 0x060E1400 at 0x0604CC90 are palette colours: the 32-entry table at 0x0604CC70 is passed to 0x0600F334 at 0x0602C4FC. They are not pointers.

C begins exactly where a 128-row table ends. The 32-byte-row random table at 0x06054424 has 128 rows, and 0x06054424 + 128*32 = 0x06055424. Its reader at 0x060256CC-0x060256EC computes row = r2 + r3. r2 is extu.b @(13,r14) or @(14,r14), chosen by player+0x48 > 30. r3 is extu.w player+0x190 when byte player+0x237 is non-zero, else 10. The read address is 0x06054424 + row*32 + (rand & 0x1F), with no clamp. Writers of player+0x190: 0x060268C8 (byte from a table at *0x060D9330), 0x0602FC34 (*0x060CFEF8 >> 16, exts.w) and 0x0602FC42 (31). Observed values are 6, 9 and 28 (end001 dumps). A row of 128 or more reads C, so C's zero bytes would be read as data. Whether the attack-record bytes at +13/+14 keep the row below 128 was not checked. Separately, 0x06055824-0x0605582F (the last 12 bytes of C) are record 0 of the 16-byte hitbox array whose pointer 0x06055824 is entry 0 of the table at 0x06057044. M2CB/M3CB overlays store that table in object field +52 (for example M2CB00A at 0x060734A0/0x060734AA, base 0x06070800). The readers at 0x060250DC and 0x060251FC compute table[0] + idx*16 but skip idx == 0 (tst/bt), so record 0 was not seen being read. The reader of the table at 0x06054024 (0x06029364) masks the row with 0x7F, so it reads no higher than 0x06055023, below C.

checked:
Static check of CYBER.BIN (base 0x0600D000), 0.BIN (base 0x060A0000) and every overlay. Method: a full disassembly at /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-colinwhite-workspace-personal-cyberbots-saturn-en-translation/0039cb9b-c04e-4750-8bf6-329b9b60dd99/scratchpad/opt003-review/cyber.dis, plus scripts lits.py, refs.py and loads.py in that folder. Found clean:
(1) Literal pointers: aligned literals into or near A, B and C in all disc files were checked. The only ones that matter are covered in the refutations. The literals in STG0A, KEND_1 and PL3E are odd or unaligned data, not referenced by code.
(2) CD loaders: 0x06038E40 takes name, destination and size, rounds up to whole sectors, and is reached through 0x060385A0. Every call in CYBER.BIN (0x06017C16, 0x06032B16, 0x06034EDE, 0x06036DCE, the table loaders at 0x06038748-0x06038984 and 0x06038B9A-0x06038D46) and in END, KEND, OPDEMO, STG0AS and VICTORY was checked. WRAM-H destinations: 0x06060000 (cap 0x32000 or 0x80000), 0x06070800 and 0x0608B000 (cap 0x80000), 0x060A6800 (PL13_0, 0x24A38), 0x060B8800 (0x13000, ends 0x060CB800), 0x060E8000 (SDDRVS1.TSK 0x6400, CONTI_0.BIN 0xE000). With real file sizes, none overlaps A, B or C. The other loaders, 0x06038F6C, 0x06038FFC and 0x060390C4, go to VDP2 at 0x05E00000, or to 0x060DEF7C for one sector, ending 0x060DF77C.
(3) SCU DMA: the only register users are 0x06016954 (ASR/AREF setup), the generic setter at 0x06040D78 and the start at 0x06040DD8. Their only code callers are 0x0603D22C (VDP1 VRAM flush, source = the command list and pattern staging) and the CD-library wrapper 0x06041D38. No SH-2 DMAC literal 0xFFFFFF8x/9x was found.
(4) Slave SH-2: it is started. 0x060169F8 calls 0x06011ECC, which runs SYS_SETSINT(0x94, 0x06011E80); the dump shows *0x06000250 = 0x06011E80. It then writes SSHON 2 through *0x06047E84 = 0x2010001F. The slave loop at 0x06011E80 runs jobs posted by 0x06010552-0x060105E2 (MINIT write to 0x21000000). Each job is 0x060103CE(dest, src, w, h), with the destination taken from the pattern allocator; the dump argument is 0x060EDC80, at or above 0x060E8000. The breakpoint logs cannot see these slave writes, but the canary would. The slave's stack is set by the BIOS and was not located. SMPC commands in CYBER.BIN and 0.BIN: 0x02, 0x06, 0x07, 0x10, 0x19 and 0x1A only.
(5) Memory next to A: BUP_Init at 0x06036824 (BIOS vector 0x06000358) uses lib 0x060E8000-0x060EC000 and work from 0x060EC000, so it starts at A's end and does not overlap. The pattern-staging allocator runs up from *0x06047D20 = 0x060E8000 and down from *0x06047D24 = 0x06100000. The base variables are only read, in CYBER.BIN and in all overlays.
(6) Stacks: CYBER.BIN's entry sets r15 = 0x06008008, and task stacks are at 0x06008000-0x0600D000. Neither touches A, B or C.
(7) BSS variables 0x060DF784-0x060DF8A4 (dumps opt001/27173 and end001/17008): none points into B. 0x060DF8A0 = 0x060DBC80, and the others point into WRAM-H BSS, SMPC or 0x25A0xxxx.
(8) A, B and C are all zero in all 18 local WRAM-H dumps. The 0x060E0EA7-0x060E1144 bytes are the same in every dump.
